query: For material-extrusion (FFF/FDM) 3D printing of polyetherimide (PEI; SABIC ULTEM 9085 and ULTEM 1010 filament, Tg about 186 C and 217 C), which build plate (print bed) material and surface treatment gives the best first-layer adhesion during printing combined with clean, damage-free part release afterwards? Compare the candidate bed surfaces reported in the literature and in printer and material-supplier documentation: polyimide (Kapton) film or tape on glass or aluminium; borosilicate glass, bare or with adhesives (PVA glue stick, PEI/ULTEM dissolved in solvent as a slurry, commercial high-temperature adhesives such as Magigoo PEEK/PEI or Vision Miner Nano Polymer Adhesive); smooth or textured PEI (ULTEM) sheets, including the risk of a PEI part fusing to a PEI bed; G10/FR4 glass-epoxy (Garolite); PEEK or polysulfone/PPSU sheets; the high-temperature build sheets and support-material rafts used by Stratasys Fortus/F900 printers for ULTEM 9085 and ULTEM 1010; carbon-fibre composite plates; and bare or coated metal (aluminium, spring steel, steel with a PEI coating). For each surface report the bed and chamber temperatures used, measured adhesion force or warpage/curling, removal behaviour, surface wear or degradation and lifetime, and the maximum continuous-use temperature of the surface itself. Conclude with a ranked recommendation, and state separately what works best when the printer's bed is limited to about 120 C and its chamber to about 65 C, versus a printer with a 160-200 C bed and a heated chamber at 150 C or more.
